decks.module: Recognize impairment without a safe-drink inference

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not rely on personal or friends' judgments.
cards.back: Do not rely on personal or friends' judgments of driving ability after drinking; impairment can occur before visible signs appear.
cards.memory_hook: Recognize impairment without a safe drink

cards.front: Complete the rule: The handbook describes alcohol moving from the stomach.
cards.back: The handbook describes alcohol moving from the stomach and small intestine into the blood and throughout the body.
cards.memory_hook: Recognize impairment without a safe drink

cards.front: Complete the rule: Food in the stomach slows the described absorption.
cards.back: Food in the stomach slows the described absorption compared with an empty stomach; it does not establish safe driving after drinking.
cards.memory_hook: Recognize impairment without a safe drink

cards.front: Complete the rule: Alcohol can dull judgment, inhibition and self-control and.
cards.back: Alcohol can dull judgment, inhibition and self-control and impair reaction, coordination, balance, vision and distance judgment.
cards.memory_hook: Recognize impairment without a safe drink

cards.front: Complete the rule: Once alcohol is in the blood, aspirin, coffee.
cards.back: Once alcohol is in the blood, aspirin, coffee, breathing exercises, a slap, physical exercise or food do not sober a person; the source identifies time as the recovery factor.

cards.back: Alcohol can change mood and create false confidence while slowing thinking and reaction.

cards.back: The handbook lists excessive speed, weaving, unusually slow travel, jerky controls and abrupt stops as possible signs of an impaired driver.

cards.back: Combining alcohol with certain medications or drugs can increase impairment and interfere with driving tasks.
